about: Contest styles to practise, each modelled on a common real format. Summaries are written for this app; check each event's own rules before entering for real.

contests.name: UK club sprint
contests.summary: Short weekday-evening sessions on 80 m between UK club members, in the style of the RSGB club championships. Send a report and a serial number; every contact scores a point.

contests.name: Serial and prefix
contests.summary: Report plus serial number, worldwide. Each new callsign prefix (G4, DL1, K9…) is a multiplier, so unusual prefixes are worth chasing.

contests.name: CQ zones
contests.summary: Report plus your CQ zone (the UK is zone 14). Zones worked are multipliers, and contacts with other continents score more.

contests.name: Work the Americas
contests.summary: Stations in the USA and Canada send their state or province; you send a report and your power. Each state or province is a multiplier.

contests.name: Field day
contests.summary: Portable stations out in the field. The exchange is the station class (number of transmitters plus a letter for the kind of station) and the operating section.

contests.name: Sweepstakes
contests.summary: The long exchange: serial number, precedence letter, callsign, check (the year first licensed, two digits) and section. Good practice for copying a lot at once.

contests.name: Weekly sprint
contests.summary: An hour-long weekly sprint in the style of the CWops tests: name and member number (or state or country). Each new call is a multiplier, and it moves fast.

contests.name: Park activation
contests.summary: You're portable in a park and the hunters find you. Ten contacts makes a valid activation in the most popular park scheme. Send a report and your park reference; they send a report and where they are.

contests.name: Summit activation
contests.summary: You've carried a small rig up a hill. Four contacts qualify the summit. Exchanges are short: calls and reports. Batteries are limited, so keep it brisk.

contests.name: DX pileup
contests.summary: You're the rare one. Everybody calls at once; pick out a callsign (or part of one), give a 5NN, and move on. Turn on split to spread the callers out above your frequency.
